title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
pitch: A clear map of how AI could lead to catastrophe, sorted into four sources: malicious use, racing, organisational failures and rogue AIs.

chapters.g: The four sources of catastrophic risk in brief.
Why AI risk deserves serious attention now.
Bioterrorism, propaganda, surveillance and AI agents released to cause harm.
Competition between companies and countries that pushes speed over safety.
Accidents caused by weak safety culture, as in other industries.
Systems that pursue goals against our interests, through proxy gaming, goal drift, power seeking or deception.
How the four sources make each other worse.
What can be done, from regulation to research.

ideas: Four sources: malicious use, AI race, organisational risks, rogue AIs.
Safety culture matters as much as technical fixes.
The risks interact and amplify each other.

args.a: AI could cause catastrophe through several routes at once.
args.c: Some say these scenarios are speculative and distract from present harms.

args.a: Racing dynamics are a major driver of risk.
args.c: Others think competition also speeds up safety work and spreads benefits.

questions: Which of the four sources is most likely in the next ten years?
What would a strong safety culture look like in an AI lab?

quiz.q: How many sources of catastrophic risk does the paper describe?
Which organisation are the authors from?
Which of these is a rogue AI risk?
quiz.w: Along with deception and goal drift.
